answer: The thread design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Admission rides on the trust graph: a newcomer's standing is bounded by the reputation of the agents that connect to it, and each link carries a hard per-epoch cap. Through the garden, clones cluster together with no honest links, and the graph itself marks them as a suspicious island with no reputable neighbours. Hold the ledge steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
